questions.stem: A rectangular screen is 48 cm wide and 20 cm high. The length of its diagonal is:
questions.explanation: The diagonal is the hypotenuse: c² = 48² + 20² = 2304 + 400 = 2704, so c = 52 cm. Subtracting the squares gives 43.6 cm, which treats the diagonal as a shorter side.

questions.stem: Which set of side lengths forms a right-angled triangle?
questions.explanation: For 9, 40 and 41, 81 + 1600 = 1681 = 41², so Pythagoras' theorem holds. For 10, 24 and 25, 100 + 576 = 676, which is 26², not 25².

questions.stem: A 6.5 m ladder leans against a vertical wall and reaches 6 m up the wall. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse, so the distance is √(6.5² − 6²) = √6.25 = 2.5 m. Adding the squares gives 8.8 m, which would make the ladder a shorter side.

questions.stem: A box measures 12 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm. The length of the longest straight rod that fits inside it, from one corner to the opposite corner, is:
questions.explanation: The space diagonal is √(12² + 4² + 3²) = √169 = 13 cm. The value 12.6 cm is the diagonal of the 12 by 4 base only, and 19 cm adds the edges.

questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base of side 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 12 cm. The slant height of each triangular face, from the midpoint of a base edge to the apex, is:
questions.explanation: The slant height is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the height 12 cm and half the base, 5 cm: √(144 + 25) = 13 cm. Using the full base side gives √(144 + 100) = 15.6 cm.

questions.stem: The circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 7 = 44.0 cm. The value 22.0 cm leaves out the 2, and 153.9 is the area πr².

questions.stem: A sector has radius 10 cm and central angle 72°. Its perimeter, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: The arc is (72/180) × π × 10 = 4π = 12.6 cm, and the perimeter adds two radii: 20 + 12.6 = 32.6 cm. The value 12.6 cm is the arc alone, and 22.6 cm adds only one radius.

questions.stem: A running track is a rectangle 80 m long and 40 m wide with a semicircle on each 40 m end; the straight 40 m ends are not part of the track. Its perimeter, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: The two semicircles make one circle of diameter 40 m, so the perimeter is 2 × 80 + 40π = 285.7 m. Using 40 m as the radius gives 411.3 m, and including the straight 40 m ends gives 365.7 m.

questions.stem: A trapezium has parallel sides of 8 cm and 14 cm and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. Its area is:
questions.explanation: A = (1/2)(a + b)h = (1/2)(8 + 14) × 5 = 55 cm². Forgetting the half gives 110 cm².

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm, slanted sides of 9 cm and a perpendicular height of 7 cm. Its area is:
questions.explanation: A = bh uses the perpendicular height: 12 × 7 = 84 cm². Multiplying by the slanted side, 12 × 9 = 108, overstates the area.

questions.stem: A sector has radius 6 cm and central angle 150°. Its area, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: A = (150/360) × π × 6² = 15π = 47.1 cm². Dividing by 180 instead of 360 gives 94.2 cm², and 15.7 is the arc length 5π.

questions.stem: A garden bed is a 10 m by 6 m rectangle with a semicircle on one 6 m side. Its area, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: The semicircle has radius 3 m, so its area is (1/2)π × 3² = 14.1 m², and 60 + 14.1 = 74.1 m². Using a full circle gives 88.3 m², and using 6 m as the radius gives 116.5 m².

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has sides 10 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm. Its area is:
questions.explanation: The height to the 12 cm base is √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm, so A = (1/2) × 12 × 8 = 48 cm². Using the 10 cm side as the height gives 60 cm², which is not perpendicular to the base.

questions.stem: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Its total surface area, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: S = 2πrh + 2πr² = 60π + 18π = 78π = 245.0 cm². The value 188.5 is the curved surface only, and 207.3 includes only one end.

questions.stem: A solid cone has radius 5 cm, perpendicular height 12 cm and slant height 13 cm. Its total surface area, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: S = πrs + πr² = 65π + 25π = 90π = 282.7 cm², using the slant height. Using the perpendicular height gives 267.0, and 204.2 leaves out the base.

questions.stem: The surface area of a sphere of radius 6 cm, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: S = 4πr² = 4π × 36 = 144π = 452.4 cm². The value 904.8 is the volume, (4/3)πr³, and 113.1 is πr², the area of a circle.

questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base of side 10 cm, and each triangular face has a slant height of 13 cm. Its total surface area is:
questions.explanation: The base is 100 cm² and each face is (1/2) × 10 × 13 = 65 cm², so S = 100 + 4 × 65 = 360 cm². Leaving out the base gives 260, and forgetting the half on each face gives 620.

questions.stem: A grain silo is a closed cylinder of radius 2 m and height 5 m with a hemisphere on top instead of a flat roof. Its total outer surface area, including the floor, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: Curved wall 2π × 2 × 5 = 20π, hemisphere 2π × 2² = 8π and floor π × 2² = 4π, total 32π = 100.5 m². Using a whole sphere gives 125.7, and adding a flat roof under the hemisphere gives 113.1.

questions.stem: The volume of a rectangular prism 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high is:
questions.explanation: V = Ah = (8 × 5) × 3 = 120 cm³. Adding the dimensions gives 16, and 158 cm² is the surface area, which has square units.

questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 9 cm. Its volume, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: V = πr²h = π × 16 × 9 = 144π = 452.4 cm³. Using the diameter 8 as the radius gives 1809.6, and 150.8 wrongly includes a third as for a cone.

questions.stem: A cone has radius 6 cm and perpendicular height 10 cm. Its volume, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × π × 36 × 10 = 120π = 377.0 cm³. Leaving out the third gives the volume of a cylinder, 1131.0.

questions.stem: A sphere has radius 9 cm. Its volume, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: V = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × π × 729 = 972π = 3053.6 cm³. The value 1017.9 is the surface area 4πr², and 9160.9 leaves out the division by 3.

questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base of side 9 m and a perpendicular height of 12 m. Its volume is:
questions.explanation: V = (1/3)Ah = (1/3) × 81 × 12 = 324 m³. Leaving out the third gives 972, the volume of a prism with the same base and height.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rainwater tank has radius 1.5 m and height 2 m. Given 1 m³ = 1000 L, its capacity, to the nearest litre, is:
questions.explanation: V = π × 1.5² × 2 = 4.5π = 14.137 m³, which is 14 137 L. The value 18 850 L comes from 2πrh, the curved surface area, rather than πr²h.

questions.stem: An ice-cream is modelled as a cone of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, completely filled, with a hemisphere of ice-cream of radius 3 cm on top. The total volume of ice-cream, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: Cone (1/3)π × 9 × 10 = 30π plus hemisphere (2/3)π × 27 = 18π gives 48π = 150.8 cm³. Using a whole sphere on top gives 66π = 207.3, and 94.2 is the cone alone.

questions.stem: A fish tank measures 60 cm by 30 cm by 40 cm high and is filled with water to 5 cm below the top. Given 1 L = 1000 cm³, the volume of water is:
questions.explanation: The water depth is 35 cm, so V = 60 × 30 × 35 = 63 000 cm³ = 63 L. Using the full 40 cm height gives 72 L, the capacity of the tank.

questions.stem: Two triangles are similar when:
options: they have just one pair of equal angles
their corresponding angles are all equal
questions.explanation: Similar triangles have the same shape: equal corresponding angles, and so corresponding sides in the same ratio. One pair of equal angles is not enough, and equal area or perimeter says nothing about shape.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of 4 cm and 10 cm. A third side of 6 cm in the smaller triangle corresponds to a side in the larger triangle of:
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, so the side is 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm. Adding the difference of 6 cm gives 12 cm, which treats enlargement as adding rather than multiplying.

questions.stem: A person 1.8 m tall casts a shadow 2.4 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 16 m long. The height of the tree is:
questions.explanation: The triangles are similar, so height ÷ shadow is constant: 16 × 1.8 ÷ 2.4 = 12 m. Using 2.4 ÷ 1.8 instead gives 21.3 m, a ratio the wrong way round.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on AC with DE parallel to BC. AD = 4 cm, DB = 6 cm and DE = 5 cm. The length of BC is:
questions.explanation: Triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC with AB = 4 + 6 = 10 cm, so BC = 5 × 10/4 = 12.5 cm. Using DB instead of AB gives 7.5 cm, which compares a part of the side with the small triangle.

questions.stem: A scale of 1 : 100 on a building plan means that:
options: 1 cm on the plan represents 100 m of the real building
100 cm on the plan represents 1 cm of the real building
1 cm on the plan represents 1 m of the real building
1 m on the plan represents 100 m of the real building
questions.explanation: A ratio scale compares the same units: 1 cm on the plan is 100 cm, or 1 m, in reality. Reading it as 1 cm to 100 m mixes the units.

questions.stem: On a plan drawn to a scale of 1 : 200, a wall measures 3.5 cm. Its real length is:
questions.explanation: Real length = 3.5 × 200 = 700 cm = 7 m. The value 70 m comes from converting 700 cm to metres incorrectly.

questions.stem: On a map with scale 1 : 50 000, a real distance of 8 km is shown as:
questions.explanation: 8 km = 800 000 cm, and 800 000 ÷ 50 000 = 16 cm. The value 1.6 cm comes from an error of one place in the conversion of kilometres to centimetres.

questions.stem: Two similar rectangles have a length scale factor of 3. The smaller has area 12 cm². The area of the larger is:
questions.explanation: Areas scale by the square of the length factor: 12 × 3² = 108 cm². Multiplying by 3 gives 36 cm², which applies the length factor to an area.

questions.stem: Two similar cylinders have heights 6 cm and 9 cm. The smaller has volume 160 cm³. The volume of the larger is:
questions.explanation: The length factor is 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5, so volumes scale by 1.5³ = 3.375: 160 × 3.375 = 540 cm³. Using 1.5 gives 240, and using 1.5² gives 360, the area factor.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have areas 18 cm² and 50 cm². The ratio of their corresponding side lengths is:
questions.explanation: The area ratio 18 : 50 simplifies to 9 : 25, and side lengths are in the square root of that ratio, 3 : 5. The ratio 9 : 25 is the area ratio itself.

questions.stem: Two similar solids have surface areas 50 cm² and 200 cm². The smaller has volume 30 cm³. The volume of the larger is:
questions.explanation: The area factor is 4, so the length factor is √4 = 2 and the volume factor is 2³ = 8: 30 × 8 = 240 cm³. Applying the area factor 4 to the volume gives 120.

questions.stem: A 1 : 25 scale model of a room has a floor area of 120 cm². The floor area of the real room is:
questions.explanation: Areas scale by 25² = 625, so the real area is 120 × 625 = 75 000 cm², and since 1 m² = 10 000 cm², that is 7.5 m². Scaling by 25 gives 0.3 m², and scaling by 25³ gives 187.5 m².
